claims.claim: A cookie is data a server sends to a browser that may be stored and sent back to the same server with later requests.
Cookies may support session management, personalization, and tracking, while modern storage APIs are recommended for general client-side data storage.
sessionStorage is partitioned by browser tab and origin and is destroyed when its tab closes, while localStorage is partitioned by origin and persists after the browser is reopened.
Web Storage set, retrieval, and removal operations are synchronous and large or intensive operations can affect responsiveness.
Third-party cookies can be used across sites to build a profile of browsing activity, creating a privacy reason to examine purpose, transparency, and user choices.
A developer should use an organization's approved security and privacy process for sensitive data rather than casually placing it in browser storage.
